I farm 28.1 mu, so I do not spread money blindly, but I also will not underfeed the land and lose yield. I always start from what worked the year before, then I adjust a little by crop and by market. On my main land I will keep the wheat-maize rotation, because with well water here in Quzhou County that is still the steady backbone. Wheat and maize are where I protect yield first, so I will put more fertilizer and water there than on mungbean or soybean. For beans, I will save some nitrogen because they carry themselves better, but I still put phosphorus and a bit of potash so the roots and pods do not stay weak. For cash crops like chrysanthemum, spinach, and cotton, I will manage more carefully because they need cleaner fields and tighter timing. I watch costs every season, but I have farmed 40 years, so I know losing one mu of yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen good field performance nearby, keep ploughing for wheat and most cash crops, use rotary tillage for some lighter crops, irrigate from the well when the crop really needs it, and keep pesticide sprays to the level that matches pest pressure instead of spraying empty air.
